#25550. What needs to happen for Manchester United to get relegated from the Premier League?

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2578 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

What needs to happen for Manchester United to get relegated from the Premier League?

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2578 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it couldn't happen, could it?
  • The table may not be telling us the whole story but it can no longer be dismissed like it can in August or September.
  • That is why Michael Carrick had to go.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it couldn't happen, could it? The answer to that is probably not but the fact that, after Sunday's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, Manchester United being relegated to the Championship is a prospect that can be discussed as anything other than rival fan fiction ought to terrify the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

A quarter of the season is gone. The table may not be telling us the whole story but it can no longer be dismissed like it can in August or September. You'll struggle to find many teams who can sincerely argue they've been mistreated by the fixture list and United are certainly not one of them. They are where they are, 18th, a point behind Coventry City and safety, and there is not much to explain that away.

That is why Michael Carrick had to go. On Wednesday morning, the 45-year-old was still taking training at the club's Carrington base but he is expected to be relieved of his duties once the United hierarchy have met in Monaco. There, the club's chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are expected to tell minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe that it is time to part ways with Carrick. Meanwhile, talks have already begun for USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino to take the helm, returning to the Premier League two and a half years after leaving Chelsea and mere months after signing a newly introduced deal with US Soccer. It would appear that unfinished business in England -- and the Old Trafford vacancy to which he has been linked for so long -- has tempted the Argentine away on the eve of the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals.

The path Pochettino is now on is one fraught with risk. And yet coaching for survival and nothing else would be the latest in a line of clumsy decisions from the Old Trafford hierarchy. Projection models such as Opta's would probably make the case that this team is dicing with danger but, with a 22% chance of relegation, will probably be fine. Bookmakers too are pretty skeptical that United's 2027-28 will encompass trips to Blackburn and Millwall with eight or so teams priced as more likely to go down than the Red Devils. That will be informed by an analytics profile that really does not suggest United are one of the three worst teams in the Premier League.

Through 10 games, a sample size where expected goals (xG) is more predictive than goals and scorelines when it comes to future results, United have an xG difference of -0.27. If there is an average team in the division, it's Carrick's. Naturally, that is not good enough for a team with their aspirations. Another 28 games putting up those underlying numbers and United will live to fight another day.

According to recent reports, suppose they don't. As anyone that saw Sunday's game can attest, events with a significantly less than 22% probability can happen all the time. A team's xG profile doesn't always capture everything. If it did, Villa would have notably fewer than their 13 points. Things could go worse for United. Let's have a look at how that might happen.

Carrick departs Old Trafford with his reputation among the fanbase still intact. He might also find that future employers look more forgivingly on his time at United. His tally of 47 points from 27 league games was bettered only by Manchester City and Arsenal, a goal difference of plus-10 putting United behind those two, Bournemouth and Brighton.

Equally, momentum had turned. With a full pre-season to establish his ideas (rather than hone Ruben Amorim's), Carrick seems to have crafted a team who are less effective in attack and more porous in defense. The 4-4-2/4-2-4 in which his team line up out of position has been easily manipulated by superior teams and structural concerns are not offset by intensity off the ball. United rank 15th for pressures applied and 10th for passes per defensive action, both measures of pressing applied by a team. Meanwhile, the attack has both been creating fewer chances -- the comeback against Villa notwithstanding -- and being more wasteful with them. It is a bad cocktail.

According to recent reports, the risk would have been that United reaffirmed the commitment they made to Carrick after the three-goal defeats to Como and Bournemouth, one which always seemed to be conditioned on the imminent international break. Could anyone parachuted in at a moment's notice have done much better than four points against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa? The November international break has always functioned as a critical point for English clubs. Fail to pull the trigger now when there is time to get your feet under the desk and familiarize yourself with players -- who, for once, will have a few days back at the training ground after their commitments around the globe -- before the festive fixture list bears its teeth. In that context, sacking a relatively inexperienced coach like Carrick probably lessens the relegation risk somewhat.

It has been revealed that so, in principle, does hiring Pochettino. Here is a coach with over 400 games at the helm of English clubs, whose first job in the country with Southampton has afforded him some experience of the tight margins needed to avoid the drop zone. It was his work at Tottenham that so enamored Sir Alex Ferguson. Over five and a half years he forged Spurs into contenders for (but not winners of) the biggest prizes in the sport. Aggressive, attacking football with a young side imbued with English talent: everything except the silverware screams Manchester United in their pomp.

The price of that success was Pochettino's identity and Tottenham's intermingling. No bad thing when you are as successful as he was at first but it may have given the Argentine an expectation about his role in club football that he has brushed up against in subsequent jobs. At Chelsea he took umbrage at the hierarchy's insistence on affording him young signings rather than the veterans he wanted. The idea that set pieces should sit somewhat outside his jurisdiction and under "specialists" was not popular. At Tottenham, Pochettino had become accustomed to working cheek to jowl with executive chairman and part-owner Daniel Levy. Chelsea, like most Premier League clubs, have established numerous layers between the man in the dugout and the owners. He may not lose his rag in the manner of Antonio Conte but Pochettino is a deeply political operator. Any man who is not afraid to say what he sees could create a great deal of friction when he sees what has been going on at United these last few years.

It has been revealed that when he left Stamford Bridge the sense was that Pochettino was yesterday's man in the rapidly evolving world of the Premier League, even though in retrospect it appears he left strong foundations for Enzo Maresca to build on. That view was clearly not one that senior figures at United entirely discounted. After all, at the time they were seriously considering sacking Erik ten Hag after finishing eighth in the Premier League. Pochettino was among the names they considered before doubling down on the soon-to-be-deposed Dutchman.

It has been revealed that that was not the only time United could have got Pochettino. Indeed, when he left Paris Saint-Germain in the summer of 2022, he was interviewed before Ten Hag got the job. That was the most formal approach but there was also the restaurant summit with Ferguson at a Mayfair restaurant when Louis van Gaal was on the brink. And of course there was the chance to hire the 54-year-old in that window earlier this year when Carrick's interim spell was coming to an end and Pochettino had not yet recommitted to the USMNT.

Sources indicate that going for a coach they have consistently decided is not the best option for them will now cost them $10 million for his compensation plus the cost of his sizeable staff. The evidence of PSG, Chelsea and the USMNT is he can deliver to (realistic) expectations. In all likelihood things stabilize under Pochettino, the specter of relegation cast off. The scenario where he takes them down? It probably reflects yesterday's man taking a job at a club still enamored with an outdated vision of management. Pochettino is probably the most Ferguson-coded manager United have employed since the great man's anointed successor. His intense style of play will need willing participants and even if he finds them, it will also take time. That much was as apparent at the clubs where it clicked -- one win in his first seven league games with Southampton, three in nine at Spurs -- as it was elsewhere. Time is not a commodity a side in 18th place can really trade in.

Though Phil Neville was quite scathing in his assessment of Noussair Mazraoui, Ayden Heaven, Leny Yoro and Diogo Dalot on Sunday -- "that back four gets you relegated" -- in pure talent terms United should be absolutely fine. You can question how many players in the squad make up the core of the title-contending outfit they aspire to be but there has been plenty of decent business done buying decent players from decent Premier League teams. Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha, (in theory right now if not in practice) Youri Tielemans.

Getting another left back and another forward in January would solve a few issues created by more injury-addled players. Then again so would the players on the roster executing better. United rank fourth in the league for non-penalty xG but 11th for goals. Maybe that is because of their wayward finishing. Opta's shooting goals added metric, which assesses the likelihood of a goal being scored pre- and post-shot, ranks this team 17th in the league on -3.57. You wouldn't expect that to hold all season long, particularly when some of the worst offenders are Bruno Fernandes and Cunha. Of course, if it did, then yes, United would be in real trouble.

According to recent reports, the same at the other end. Yoro met a free kick with a fine header at Old Trafford on Sunday, drawing a springy save from a goalkeeper who could not stop the ball being turned in on the rebound. The slight problem is the goalkeeper was Senne Lammens and that was the fourth error leading to a goal that United have made this season. Low-volume statistics like these can occasionally betray you but in this case it speaks to a truth clear for all to see; the United defense is too slap-dashy. Young and old, players at Old Trafford have learned that basic errors rarely lead to lasting consequences. If this clumsiness continues -- and it should not be treated as a given that it does -- then the crisis could deepen.

It's worth saying from the off that if you're rooting for chaos you'd want to see Manchester United's numbers trend down quite dramatically for there to be much in the analytics that indicates 18th or worse. The "best" relegated sides of recent years are probably Leicester City in 2022-23, sent down to the Championship on 34 points and -0.39 non-penalty xG difference (npxGD) per game, and West Ham three years later. They slipped through the trap door on 39 points and -0.26 npxGD, just a shade worse than Tottenham. Manchester United have sunk to levels below that in past seasons but not this.

Right now there is a long way to go to catch up with the worst teams in the league so far. Ipswich Town have accrued points and look to be a hard out but they are averaging -0.67 npxG difference per game. They are the worst of the newly promoted sides but both Hull City (-0.5) and Coventry City (-0.48) are delivering worrying analytics. The former have the advantage of those points they accrued early in the season and Hull deserve credit for how sparky and organized they are given the talent deficit Sergej Jakirovic is working with. Apply some of those principles with United's talent and competence is no longer the limit.

It isn't just the promoted sides that look bad. Sunderland have a case of difficult second-season syndrome. The best that can be remarked for Newcastle is that, like Hull, they've banked some fortuitous points. We can maybe ignore Aston Villa given how rarely their xG reflects the results Unai Emery gets.

In a recent development, then there is Crystal Palace and, well, yikes. In the six seasons before this one only seven teams have had a worse npxGD per game than Palace's -0.86, which is a true marker of inadequacy. These levels Pierre Sage has plummeted the Conference League winners to aren't much better than Norwich City in 2021-22, Luton Town in 2023-24 or the carnival of ineptitude that was Leicester and Southampton two years ago. Palace are bad. So, so bad.

At least they are in results terms. The talent doesn't seem that bad even if the drip-drip of departures over the last year -- Oliver Glasner, Maxence Lacroix, Marc Guehi, Eberechi Eze -- has lowered their ceiling. With a Thomas Frank in charge you could see them move back on the right path quickly. Maybe the northeast triumvirate swing upwards too. Suddenly then there might be a space opening up for a team that is both bad and unlucky. That is, of course, assuming that there are three spots opened up for relegated teams this season.

According to recent reports, of course Manchester City might yet have a spot in next season's Championship with their name on it. City were found to have breached 114 of the Premier League's rules by an independent commission, a verdict they are in the midst of appealing.

Sources indicate that separate to the process of establishing whether the commission erred in its duties is the matter of sanctioning City. That will be decided by the same three-person panel though it is not yet clear when the hearing will take place nor what the Premier League will expect. Given the abrasive language used by the league about one of its member clubs, it is hard to see them settling for a proposal that does not end with City out of the top flight at the end of the season.

The Premier League wants this process wrapped up comprehensively but swiftly. Much of the football world expects City to get hit hard, hence why bookmakers have Enzo Maresca's side among the three most likely teams to be relegated. A sweeping points deduction at the Etihad Stadium would be greeted with delight around Old Trafford for many reasons. The fact that it might insulate United from their own mismanagement is certainly one of them.

It has been revealed that there are, however, no guarantees that this process will reach its conclusion before the end of the season. City could endure, dragging out a process they have made plain they believe to be compromised at its most basic principles. Can they keep the wheels spinning for another seven-plus months? Or argue their way to the sort of punishment that does not send them off the edge of the Premier League map? It may be hard to do but it is the sort of unlikely event that, for the time being, might be required to send United to the Championship.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United midfielder Jacob Ramsey has offered an honest assessment of his struggles at St James’ Park, admitting his spell on Tyneside has not met expectations following his £ 43 million move from Aston Villa.

The 25-year-old joined the Magpies in the summer of 2025 but has struggled to establish himself as a regular starter, with injuries and disciplinary problems disrupting his progress.

According to a report via Birmingham Mail, Ramsey has acknowledged a disappointing start at Newcastle but remains determined to show his qualities under latest manager Matthias Jaissle.

Sources indicate that speaking about his experience, the midfielder admitted that several promising moments have been followed by frustrating setbacks. He highlighted his impressive contribution against Bournemouth, where he scored after coming off the bench, only to suffer another injury shortly afterwards.

He noted: “My time here hasn’t been great; there have been certain moments where I have looked like I am about to kick on.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United are looking to sign a striker for latest manager Mauricio Pochettino in January, and they have already got the green light from one of the best in the world over a move to Old Trafford if the deal is right.

Man United's main concerns this season have been defensively, with no club in the top five European leagues conceding more than the 30 goals they have in all competitions this term.

The Red Devils were planning an overhaul of their backline next summer having carried out extensive work on the attack and midfield in the previous two transfer windows, but they may have to bring forward those plans given how poor the club has been defensively in 2026-27 so far.

United look to need upgrades all across the back four, while there is no guarantee that Luke Shaw, Lisandro Martinez and Harry Maguire will still be at Old Trafford beyond this season given their contracts expire at the end of June.

According to GIVEMESPORT sources, the Red Devils hold an interest in Fulham duo Calvin Bassey and Antonee Robinson, with the former able to play in two positions the club are looking at strengthening, centre-back and left-back.

Chelsea defender Malo Gusto is also 'one to watch' in terms of United, with the Blues willing to sell, although they valued the Frenchman at £75m as recently as the summer.

Centre-forward is the other big priority for club chiefs in the winter, with GMS revealing previously that there was interest in Dominic Calvert-Lewin at Leeds, although the England international is expected to sign a upcoming contract to stay at Elland Road.

It will be difficult for United to sign a new striker in the January transfer window, which is renowned as a seller's market rather than a buyer's one, but according to journalist Rahman Osman they may have found a top striker who's keen to join, Galatasaray's Victor Osimhen.

The report states that the Nigeria international is flattered by recent speculation linking him with a switch to Old Trafford, and he'd be ready to listen to offers from them.

There is absolutely no doubt that Pochettino would sign Harry Kane tomorrow if he had the opportunity to, but that isn't going to happen after he won the Ballon d'Or and extended his contract with Bayern Munich.

Kane is a happy spot right now that has led him to football's greatest individual prize, and he has no need to return to the Premier League, yet at least.

Kane, one of the greatest strikers in Premier League history, has made no secret of how influential Pochettino has been in his playing career, and his two best seasons in terms of Premier League goals scored came under the Argentine's leadership.

A proper goalscoring centre-forward has become more of a rarity in recent years, in a world where Kane and Erling Haaland have excelled.

There is another experienced striker putting up ridiculous numbers too in Osimhen though, one of the best strikers in world football right now, who has been outstanding for Galatasaray ever since leaving Napoli for Turkey, scoring 69 goals in 85 appearances.

The Nigeria international was one of the main reasons Napoli ended their 33-year Scudetto drought when they won the Serie A title in 2023, and he has carried on that influence in Istanbul.

Osimhen, described as a 'Top 3 striker in the world' by Alvaro Morata, is a talisman who has so many different skill sets as a striker, and he would be ready to make an instant impact at Old Trafford.

The report claims that while the soon-to-be 28-year-old would be willing to listen to United proposals, he would want to earn a similar number to the £13m-per-year he is on at Galatasaray, who could demand between £80-100m to sell their star player.

Those are two big hurdles to overcome for a club that is looking to run more sensibly, but Osimhen has shown at his previous two clubs that he could be a game-changing signing.

เมื่อต้องตัดสินใจว่า เว็บแทงบอลไหนดีสุด ในปี 2026 สิ่งสำคัญที่มองข้ามไม่ได้เลยคือ “ราคาน้ำ” (Odds) เพราะราคาน้ำคือตัวกำหนดผลกำไรและช่วยเซฟเงินทุนของคุณโดยตรง การเลือกเว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด ที่เปิดราคาบอล 4 ตังค์ คืนค่าคอมมิชชั่นสูง จะช่วยให้ทำกำไรระยะยาวจากการแทงบอลออนไลน์ ได้คุ้มค่าที่สุด หากคุณสมัครแทงบอล บนเว็บแทงบอล เชื่อถือได้ มักจะมีตัวเลือกประเภทค่าน้ำให้ปรับใช้ตามสไตล์การเดิมพัน ซึ่งแต่ละแบบมีความแตกต่างกันดังนี้.

สำหรับมือใหม่ที่ยังลังเลว่า แทงบอลออนไลน์ เว็บไหนดี ให้ทำเงินได้ไวและเสี่ยงน้อยที่สุด หัวใจสำคัญคือการเลือกรูปแบบการเดิมพันบนเว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด ให้เหมาะกับทุนและเทคนิคของตัวเอง เพราะบนเว็บแทงบอลออนไลน์ ยุคนี้ไม่ได้มีแค่การทายผลแพ้ชนะทั่วไป การเข้าใจ 5 รูปแบบยอดฮิตก่อนสมัครแทงบอล จะช่วยให้คุณวางแผนทำกำไรได้แม่นยำยิ่งขึ้น.

การเลือกเว็บแทงบอล ออนไลน์ เว็บไหนดี ที่รองรับระบบ ฝาก-ถอน Auto และ True Money Wallet ควรพิจารณาเว็บตรงที่มีความน่าเชื่อถือ ได้มาตรฐานสากล และปรับอัตราค่าน้ำคงที่.

การคัดเลือกโปรโมชั่นคุ้มค่า ถือเป็นตัวช่วยเพิ่มทุนชั้นดี แต่หากเลือกโดยไม่เช็กเงื่อนไขให้ถี่ถ้วน เครดิตฟรีที่ได้มาอาจกลายเป็นภาระในการถอนเงิน การพิจารณา เว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด จึงต้องดูควบคู่กับความยากง่ายของเงื่อนไขการทำยอดหมุนเวียน (Turnover) ด้วย.

ยอดเดิมพันสะสมรวมทั้งหมด (ได้+เสีย) ที่ระบบกำหนดให้คุณต้องเล่นให้ครบตามเกณฑ์ก่อนถอนเงินออก.

สูตรคำนวณ: (เงินฝาก + โบนัส) x จำนวนเท่าเทิร์น = ยอดเดิมพันสะสมที่ต้องทำ.

สำหรับนักเดิมพันยุคใหม่ที่เน้นความสะดวกและต้องการแทงบอลออนไลน์ ผ่านมือถือ คำถามสำคัญคือจะเลือก แทงบอลเว็บไหนดี ที่หน้าเว็บไม่ค้าง และไม่ต้องเสียเวลาตามหา วิธีแทงบอลในเว็บ หรือค้นหาทางเข้าใหม่ทุกครั้งที่ลิงก์โดนบล็อก การเลือกเว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด ที่รองรับแอปพลิเคชันโดยตรง จะช่วยแก้ปัญหานี้ได้อย่างเด็ดขาด.

การวิเคราะห์บอลกับการเลือกเว็บบอร์ดหรือ เว็บแทงบอลออนไลน์ เป็นสองปัจจัยที่ต้องทำงานควบคู่กัน หากวิเคราะห์แม่นยำแต่เลือกเว็บที่ไม่มีประสิทธิภาพหรืออัตราราคาค่าน้ำเสียเปรียบ โอกาสทำกำไรระยะยาวก็จะลดลงอย่างมาก.

การคัดเลือกแทงบอลเว็บไหนดี ในปี 2026 เพื่อให้ได้เว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด เชื่อถือได้ หัวใจสำคัญที่สุดคือการเดิมพันกับเว็บตรงไม่ผ่านเอเย่นต์ การันตีความปลอดภัย 100% การเลือกเว็บพนันบอล ดีที่สุด จะช่วยให้คุณสมัครเว็บบอล และวางเดิมพันได้อย่างมั่นใจ ถอนเงินได้จริงทุกยอดบิล.

หากคุณยังสงสัยว่า สมัครแทงบอล เว็บไหนดี การเลือกระหว่าง 8 แบรนด์ชั้นนำ (UFA248, UFA246, SAWAN168, UFA289, UFAPLUS, KO888, SAWAN246, KO789) ตามคำแนะนำจากผู้เล่นจริงในกระทู้ เว็บพนันบอล ดีที่สุด Pantip, Google, Facebook หรือ Tiktok จะเป็นทางเลือกที่ปลอดภัย คุ้มค่า และตอบโจทย์การทำกำไรได้จริงชัวร์ 100%.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United are reportedly facing questions over their recruitment strategy after Matthias Jaissle recommended Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, only for the club to pursue and sign Ederson Gonzalez instead.

The Magpies have been looking to strengthen their midfield options, with greater physicality, experience and tactical discipline becoming key considerations for their recruitment team.

In a recent development, according to a Daily Mail report, Jaissle identified Hojbjerg as a suitable addition and recommended the experienced Danish international to Newcastle. However, the club ultimately decided to move in a different direction, opting to bring Gonzalez into their squad instead.

The decision raises questions about whether Newcastle overlooked an opportunity to secure a proven midfielder who could have made an immediate difference.

It has been revealed that hojbjerg has considerable experience at the highest level, having previously represented clubs such as Tottenham and Marseille. His ability to dictate the tempo of matches, protect the defensive line, and contribute to build-up play makes him an attractive option for clubs seeking greater midfield stability.

The situation is particularly concerning given that Newcastle have lost influential midfielders Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, leaving a significant gap in terms of experience and leadership.

It has been revealed that gonzalez arrived from Manchester City on a £60 million deal, but his performances have reportedly fallen short of expectations. Newcastle had hoped that the Spaniard would provide the quality needed to compensate for their departures, but his adaptation has not gone according to blueprint.

However, Newcastle must remain mindful of their financial restrictions, meaning the recruitment department will need to identify affordable targets who can deliver an immediate impact.

The Magpies cannot afford another expensive recruitment gamble, particularly with their summer investments yet to produce the desired results.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The best American coach in Major League Soccer and someone who also got my vote for Coach of the Year after leading Nashville SC to a league-record 77 points in the regular season, B.J.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, with Mauricio Pochettino looking like he is on the way to Manchester United, there could be a major vacancy to fill for the U.S. men's national team with the head coach position. With a upcoming national training center, an established team, and young players coming up from everywhere to push that squad, it's a job that should be an attractive one to managers around the world, depending on the direction that U.S. Soccer wants to go.

Pochettino was an appropriate splash hire ahead of the World Cup, and it's not surprising that a top team in the world still wanted him. But when looking to build a stable base for 2030, there's a chance that the powers that be would prefer a candidate who would be more bought into American soccer, so when looking at potential candidates to take the role, it makes sense to sound out both options, and here's the list it has come to:.

The best American coach in Major League Soccer and someone who also got my vote for Coach of the Year after leading Nashville SC to a league-record 77 points in the regular season, B.J. Callaghan will need to be among the top contenders for the USMNT job if the U.S. Soccer Federation chooses to go with an American fit instead of another splash hire like Pochettino. He already has experience coaching and leading the USMNT during tournament play, leading the squad to the 2023 Concacaf Nations League title before heading to Nashville and turning them into one of the most complete sides in MLS. Callaghan has paid his dues, going from the college ranks all the way to the professional ones, and is someone with intimate knowledge of the American soccer system. If looking to go in a more traditional direction while also not shifting the vision of Olympic play, Callaghan is a solid choice.

According to recent reports, while Nancy's time at Celtic after leaving the Columbus Crew was a moment to forget, not all of that was his fault, as the French manager has done nothing but succeed in his career, no matter where he has gone. Limit his resources, and he'll develop a system to get the best out of what he has; increase them, and he'll go toe to toe with everyone, and that flexibility is critical in international play. It's rare that you have your first-choice 11 available, and being able to work around that is what can make a difference on the margins. Nancy could want to still test himself in Europe but it doesn't hurt to call.

Currently overseeing the U-23s, the former Los Angeles FC manager would likely be in the USMNT succession strategy for Pochettino. The goal was to bring both camps together as much as possible and ensure that they had a similar style, as plenty of players would go between both squads depending on needs. The issue is that this has all happened faster than anyone would've anticipated, since if Steve Cherundolo was going to take over the USMNT, that'd likely be a 2028 post-Olympic deal rather than right at this moment. But also looking at the performance of LAFC without Cherundolo, it's clear that he held things together plenty in that squad and that he could be a fit for the role; the question is just when.

In a recent development, you have to make the call, and it looks like they will. We all know what the answer likely is, but if there's an opening and the USMNT wants the best manager available, Pep Guardiola is right there. The former Manchester City, Bayern Munich and Barcelona boss is expected to be their top target, according to The Athletic.

In a recent development, they reportedly called Jurgen Klopp before hiring Pochettino, and this would be a similar scenario as Klopp is now with Germany. Guardiola isn't going to stay out of management forever, so why not try to bring him back in on the road to 2030? He would be facing similar issues to Pochettino of not knowing if he'll be a long-term fit for the role, but those aren't things that should come into play if the goal is to hire the best available manager who is a fit for the job.

Sources indicate that A name that came up after the World Cup when decisions were being made on whether Pochettino should be extended, Roberto Martinez could come into consideration yet again. On paper, he offers a mix of European experience and the staying power of someone who has overseen multiple international sides for an entire cycle, but it's tough to say he'd be a good fit. Martinez wasn't able to lead Belgium's golden generation to a title and struggled to get Portugal to play to their talent as well. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.

Although Celtic entered the international break on the back of victories over Besiktas and Kilmarnock, the upturn in results didn’t quite lead to an outbreak of unbridled joy along Kerrydale Street.

Since the first act of this season, a narrow win over Dundee, Martin O’Neill’s side have occupied a place of uncertainty.

Those who have taken the occasional stellar display to be indicative of a corner being turned have been left feeling like fools.

It has been revealed that there remain too many shortcomings in the squad, too many question marks hovering above too many players to ever feel that it has left inconsistency behind. The fan base has good reason not to quite trust it.

How could it be otherwise when the clean sheet claimed against bottom side Killie was the first in seven matches?

Kasper Hogh, the club’s record signing at £11million, hasn’t scored in his last 16 outings in green and white.

Martin O'Neill admits it has taken longer than he'd have liked for the upcoming recruits to settle.

O’Neill’s options on the flanks include one player in Jota, who’s getting back from a long-term injury, and another in Yang Hyun-jun, who was recently sidelined for six weeks.

There’s a veteran in James Forrest, Seb Tounekti, not exactly the bravest of souls, and Haissem Hassan, a £6m signing who evidently believes defensive work is optional.

It claims much that Callum Osmand, a centre-forward now trying to cut it on the flank, has become a fans’ favourite after just 13 senior appearances.

The concerns of the manager now extend to the middle of the park where Mika Baur may be out for up to 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage.

With Benjamin Nygren also a doubt to face St Mirren, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan and/or Joel van den Berg could be teamed up with skipper Callum McGregor.

We’re assuredly about to discover if this squad has more about it than the results and performances to this stage have suggested.

‘We can make significant improvements, there’s no question about it,’ said the manager.

‘Top of the league, it is nice to be in that position. But other than a number of matches where I think we’ve played very, very well... maybe the Besiktas game, maybe the Hearts game, it’s been really hard work for us.

‘That’s maybe a combination of things. Young and slightly more experienced players coming into the football club, getting to know the club, getting to know the players.

‘That’s taken a bit of time. I didn’t expect it to work immediately overnight.

German midfielder Mika Baur is set to miss around 10 weeks with an ankle ligament injury.

‘But they’re at a club where settling in is something they’ve got to do pretty rapidly.’.

Starting with the visit of the Paisley men, Celtic have 10 games up to and including the trip to Ibrox on January 3.

That encompasses two assignments on the road in the Europa League — Torreense and Omonia Nicosia.

O’Neill’s men also visit Tynecastle, Dens Park, Pittodrie and Tannadice in the league.

As they prepare to put up the Christmas decorations on the Celtic Way, O’Neill could privately be forgiven for wishing the festive season away.

January 5 is the day on which the transfer window in Scotland opens and you can’t help but wonder what Celtic’s prospects for the season will look like at that point.

While Camilo Duran and Baur have contributed, the bulk of the business done in the summer again looks to have been sub-standard.

To stand a chance of retaining the title, O’Neill badly needs several major-hitters to come in without delay in the Upcoming Year.

It has been revealed that ‘We’re absolutely looking at players now,’ he stressed. ‘I suppose every single club is doing that. And the quicker you can get somebody in, the better.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We’ve seen when people are fit, we will have numbers. We just need a bit of quality.’.

Camilo Duran has been one of very few summer arrivals to have made an impact at Celtic.

Until such time as he can call for the cavalry, O’Neill has no choice but to make do and mend.

On the chances of prioritising the league and playing a weakened side in Europe, the veteran is clear.

‘Domestic football is really notable to the football club, of course,’ he said. ‘But you’d still want to try and make some show in Europe. And we’ve found that difficult.

‘I genuinely thought against Besiktas we did really fine in the game, we didn’t over-press because they could play through you.

‘There are certain moments even in domestic football when teams can play through you. Kilmarnock caused us plenty of problems.

In a recent development, ‘I just think we’ve got to improve in the domestic games. We’ve got to be more aggressive in the sense of taking games to people and being less passive in periods of games.’.

O’Neill clearly needs more — much more — from so many individuals if he’s to get through the shark-infested waters of the next six weeks unscathed.

Hassan didn’t even make the matchday squad for Kilmarnock, a move which was interpreted by many as being a boot up the backside by a boss who’s been underwhelmed by his work without the ball.

‘We left out a number of players,’ O’Neill stressed. ‘I wouldn’t read as much into that, because a few will come back.

‘My job is not to please everyone, otherwise we’d have 26 players playing at one time.

O'Neill has backed misfiring striker Kasper Hogh to end his barren streak in front of goal.

‘I did a thing with corporate fans the other night, we had a bit of fun with some questions.

‘Apparently something came out that he [Hassan] was the most unpopular player in the dressing room, which is not true.

According to recent reports, ‘I didn’t say this. I was joking about my own unpopularity, as a player, because all I did was moan.

In a recent development, ‘I did say about unpopularity, there’s at least one more unpopular. The crowd wanted to know but I didn’t tell them! I left it hanging. But it was tongue-in-cheek, apart from the part about me being unpopular, which I was.’.

The form of Hogh is no laughing matter. The Dane looked the part when he claimed a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on August 9, but that is beginning to feel like ancient history.

For his effort against the Ayrshiremen a fortnight ago to be ruled out for an earlier infringement by Baur was a low blow.

In a recent development, ‘For him, that was a killer,’ O’Neill reflected. ‘He has got the goal, gone off and celebrated and you just think... oh no, is that a goal?

Industry observers note that ‘He has worked exceptionally hard for us. But strikers live by goals and at some stage or other, he needs a goal.

‘The best thing for me to do is bring Henrik Larsson over and show him how to hit the ball into the net.

‘Shaun Maloney was telling me that for a little period he played up front when Henrik was injured for about a month.

It has been revealed that ‘And Henrik in that time was giving him advice about how centre-halves were reading him. He told him about getting yourself room, losing the centre-half, don’t be fighting with him all the time.

‘He scored a bag full of goals, so there must be something in it.’.

#25537. Breaking: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (825 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Janosch, the pen name of German author and illustrator Horst Eckert, won hearts around the world with his warm and simple sense of humor.
  • Janosch created more than 150 books, which have been translated into over 30 languages.
  • His best-selling children's book, "Oh, wie schön ist Panama," translated into English as "The Trip to Panama," was so lucrative that Janosch was able to settle down on the Canary Island of Tenerife in 1980, where he lived together with his wife Ines.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Janosch, the pen name of German author and illustrator Horst Eckert, won hearts around the world with his warm and simple sense of humor. He charmed children and adults alike with his iconic Tiger, Bear, Tiger-Duck and other animals.

Janosch created more than 150 books, which have been translated into over 30 languages.

His best-selling children's book, "Oh, wie schön ist Panama," translated into English as "The Trip to Panama," was so lucrative that Janosch was able to settle down on the Canary Island of Tenerife in 1980, where he lived together with his wife Ines. The writer and illustrator died peacefully at the age of 95, his publisher Bernhard Feil announced on Wednesday.

Janosch was born as Horst Eckert on March 11, 1931, in Hindenburg (now Zabrze, Poland) in what was then Upper Silesia. After World War II, his family had to flee to Germany.

In 1953, Janosch started studying at the Academy of Art in Munich, thinking that it would be easy to become an artist. He was however dismissed after just a few terms for "lack of talent.".

Sources indicate that but luckily for his later readers, Janosch did not give up. He continued to work as a freelance artist, soon discovering his second great gift, namely writing.

His first children's book about a horse named Valek was published in 1960.

Although Janosch became famous primarily for his children's books, he also wrote books for adults that focused on his own childhood.

Even though he wrote cheerful books for children, Janosch hardly had any positive memories of his own childhood, as his father was an alcoholic. He was beaten not only by him but also by his mother and grandmother. Raised in a strictly Catholic environment, he was continuously threatened to be punished by God.

Later on, Janosch tried to overcome the burden of his childhood memories by turning to alcohol as well.

He always expressed a great deal of understanding for children, trying to encourage them to stand up for their rights. As a result of his childhood experiences, Janosch did not want to have children himself, and his attitude towards the Catholic Church always remained divided. "As I am a sinner and a heretic, God will let me live a long life so that I can return to the Church," he told his biographer Angela Bajorek.

Recent findings suggest that janosch's animal figures are endearing but not always well-behaved. They love all kinds of nonsense. But even if they lie to each other or put their own interests first, the true winner at the end of stories is always friendship and solidarity.

Janosch achieved his major breakthrough with "The Trip to Panama," a story about two friends, a little tiger and a bear, who set out to find their paradise in Panama. After touring around in circles, they finally end up where they started out; they realize that their journey was the destination. Janosch received the German Youth Book Prize in 1979 for the work.

Janosch's protagonists have become familiar to generations of children all over the world. They come up over and over again in the various stories carefully illustrated with water colors.

There is the honest lion Hans from the toy chest who fails to catch a nutcracker with his lies. There is Schnuddel and a ridiculous bragger Günter the Box-Frog. And then there is a tiger that collects mushrooms while looking out for his devoted friend, a bear, who always stands up for him even when the tiger temporarily leaves him because of a little pig in one of the stories.

Recent findings suggest that the "Tigerente," literally "Tiger-Duck," a wooden duck on wheels with yellow-brown stripes, appears on numerous pictures by the illustrator. At times, the animal has been tossed into a corner, at times it is hanging from the ceiling, or the Box-Frog pulls it across the drawing.

It has been revealed that his iconic figures, especially the Tiger-Duck, have served as motifs on various items, from cups to stamps to jewelry, and even on airplanes. Film adaptations and TV series based on his stories were produced in German and English.

Guests who visited Janosch in Tenerife were impressed by his very modest lifestyle. He always said that hanging around in his hammock doing nothing was what he enjoyed most. And yet Janosch remained very active until the end of his life.

From 2013 to 2019, he wrote a column for the German weekly Die Zeit, taking on the role of Mr. Wondrak, who commented on world affairs. Shortly before his 90th birthday in 2021, the complete collection of his Mr. Wondrak columns were published as a book in German.

In a recent development, like the protagonists in his stories, Janosch always tried to content himself with few things. As he wrote in one of his books: "He who needs almost nothing, has everything.".

This article was originally written in German.

Celtic have suffered a major blow on the injury front following the news that Mika Baur faces a lengthy spell out of action.

Injuring his ankle in Celtic's 1-0 win over Kilmarnock just prior to November's international break, the 22-year-old is looking at around ten weeks on the sidelines, meaning it could be February by the time he is involved once again.

The injuries to the first-choice midfielders will see Martin O'Neill have to switch things about in the middle of the park, thus potentially opening the door for Luke McCowan, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain or even Oliver Sorensen to come into the team.

Given the injury news regarding Baur and Nygren, some Celtic fans have made the point that Paulo Bernardo should be at the club and involved in the first team rather than spending the season on loan in Poland with Gornik Zabrze.

The 24-year-old midfielder is featuring regularly during his time in Poland, playing 17 games and assisting two goals in the process.

At a time when Celtic are now short on midfield options, O'Neill will have to come up with a plan to ensure his team remain on track and maintain their four-point lead over fierce rivals Rangers.

Paulo Bernardo's 2026/27 season in numbers.

Bernardo's current club in Poland is owned by none other than former Germany striker Lukas Podolski.

“The most crucial thing is that Bernardo feels good with us. We’ll see after the season.

Sources indicate that “Sometimes a player helps the club for a season and then leaves. Like Lubik, for example. Or maybe Celtic will need Bernardo after a good season at Gornik? All kinds of scenarios are possible here.

#25531. Inside Gotham FC's move to Icahn Stadium: Debates over pitch quality, fines and the NWSL's logistical struggle

Inside Gotham FC's move to Icahn Stadium: Debates over pitch quality, fines and the NWSL's logistical struggle

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2210 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Juan Carlos Amoros is always subtle in demeanor, down to his usual all-black attire, so after Gotham FC's uninspiring 1-0 win over the Seattle Reign on Sunday, his subdued tone was hardly a surprise.
  • "I feel the obligation to almost apologize for the state of the pitch," Amoros noted.
  • It has been revealed that he was hardly the only one to mention the grass at Sports Illustrated Stadium.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Juan Carlos Amoros is always subtle in demeanor, down to his usual all-black attire, so after Gotham FC's uninspiring 1-0 win over the Seattle Reign on Sunday, his subdued tone was hardly a surprise. His post-match remarks, though, were a departure from the victory lap a coach might take after winning in the NWSL quarterfinals.

"I feel the obligation to almost apologize for the state of the pitch," Amoros noted. "I think at this level, in this kind of game, as a league, we should be having a better surface. Unfortunately, our football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn't but luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt and the game was what it was.".

It has been revealed that he was hardly the only one to mention the grass at Sports Illustrated Stadium. It seeped its way into every post-match media availability, dominated conversation between the players and was a talking point amongst staff working that day. A dull stretch of grass with yellow-green splotches overshadowed one of the most important matches of the NWSL's season – and put the league on course for an unlikely downsize for Sunday's playoff semifinal between Gotham and the Kansas City Current.

Roughly 24 hours after Amoros' apology, Gotham moved Sunday's game to Icahn Stadium, a 5,000-seater on Manhattan's Randall's Island that they have played at just twice before. Sports Illustrated Stadium, the 25,000-seat venue in Harrison, N.J. that Gotham have called home since 2021, was available but concerns about player safety prompted an unwanted last-minute move.

It has been revealed that "We as a team worked extremely hard to earn a home playoff berth," Gotham captain Tierna Davidson said in a statement on Monday. "What we got was a field that is not the standard this club, this league or our fans deserve. The quality of the game is not up for debate, so we've made the difficult decision to move to Icahn Stadium on Sunday. A smaller stadium means many of you will not be there, and that is the hardest part of this decision.".

Monday's announcement was the final stage of a back-and-forth between Gotham and MLS' Red Bull New York, the primary tenants and operators of Sports Illustrated Stadium, one that highlights the logistical nightmares that have unexpectedly disrupted the NWSL's postseason.

MLS' World Cup break this summer afforded RBNY the chance to install a newly introduced pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, the process complete by the team's July 25 loss to Charlotte FC. It was the perfect time for a reset ahead of a busy schedule for the new field – 17 other matches were a guarantee, while the potential postseason runs for both RBNY and Gotham meant the number could stretch well over 20 games before the year was over.

Industry observers note that by the time Gotham had secured a home quarterfinal with a draw against Angel City on Oct. 4, there was little reason to suspect that the playing surface would become an problem. Matches are rarely relocated because of pitch quality concerns and the field at Sports Illustrated Stadium has historically been one of American soccer's best; it won the Sports Turf Management Association's award for professional soccer fields in 2021, the year Gotham moved in. The NWSL team did not have another home game until Nov. 1, a period in which RBNY played three home games and the stadium hosted a USA Rugby Fall Series doubleheader. Sometime before the early November fixture against the Royals, Gotham raised concerns with their landlords about the field conditions, the scars of the rugby games on Oct. 30 notably visible.

Nothing came of those complaints, though, and so the Royals match went on as scheduled but the conditions did not go unnoticed. The NWSL imposed a $10,000 fine on Gotham for the state of the field, even though they do not manage the venue as secondary tenants. The fine was not widely known – the NWSL Players Association said it was unaware of the punishment, while a source with knowledge of the matter said RBNY also did not know. Many found out about the fine after Reign head coach Laura Harvey mentioned it in a post-match press conference after the quarterfinal, but worry about the quality of the grass had already reached a fever pitch at that point.

Despite the fine, a field consultant working on the NWSL's behalf inspected the pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium on Friday and declared that it met FIFA standards. The following day, RBNY hosted their regular season finale against Atlanta United and less than 18 hours later, another group took a look at the field in the hours building up to Gotham's win over the Reign. It was deemed playable on Sunday morning by representatives from the NWSL, the Professional Referee Organization and the NWSLPA, according to a source familiar with the situation.

Recent findings suggest that even from a distance, the grass appeared problematic. The sand that was left over from the rugby doubleheader still lined the pitch, while some rugby lines were faint but visible in certain spots. The players' review of the surface, though, was damning – Harvey called it "s---," Reign captain Jess Fishlock remarked it was "atrocious," and Gotham midfielder Jaelin Howell described it as "sandy" and "unstable." Gotham attacker Jaedyn Shaw also expressed concern that her planted foot would slip during corner kicks and all agreed that it ultimately impacted the teams' ability to compete.

lower bowl isn’t quite full at kickoff between Gotham and the Seattle Reign, though there are some fans in the upper bowlGotham announced earlier that they sold 3,000 tickets through NYC Mayor Mamdani’s offer (including 1,000 in the first 10 minutes of sale)#NWSL pic.twitter.com/qviBM65bsz.

Sources indicate that gotham, in conjunction with the NWSL, spent the hours after their quarterfinal win discussing options with RBNY to improve the playing surface. The main solutions, according to multiple sources, were re-sodding the pitch – essentially ripping the existing field out and installing a new one – or a hybrid model in which artificial threads would be stitched into the existing grass. Both would be timely endeavors – the former would be longer while the latter might have been completed in time for Gotham to host the Current on Sunday.

There was just one problem. RBNY have a friendly against Club America scheduled for Saturday.

In a recent development, the game will serve as the final match of their season after they missed the MLS Cup playoffs and takes place during the men's international break, which means some players from both teams will be tied up with their national teams instead. Multiple sources said the NWSL could not guarantee that the hybrid model project would not actually be completed in time for RBNY's friendly on Saturday evening, even if it would have been ready in time for Gotham's Sunday afternoon game against the Current. RBNY were unwilling to proceed with the hybrid blueprint, as a result, and so Gotham chose to leave Sports Illustrated Stadium for Icahn Stadium.

RBNY still intend to play on the pitch that NWSL players complained about on Saturday and no changes to the field are expected to be made beforehand.

"We understand how frustrating the move is for Gotham and their fans. We had hoped to see Gotham continue its championship run at Sports Illustrated Stadium, too," RBNY said in a statement. "We invest in the pitch year-round, with a dedicated grounds team and specialist field partners, and it was cleared for every match played there this season. Those inspections continue for all remaining events this year. We worked closely with Gotham and the NWSL to address their concerns, but unfortunately the experts and the league couldn't guarantee the additional work they wanted to be completed could be done in time. We wish Gotham the best in their match.".

Sources indicate that the venue is not brand upcoming to Gotham, who have hosted two games at the stadium in the last two years, and seems well-equipped to at least solve the main problem they faced at Sports Illustrated Stadium. Amoros complimented the quality of Icahn Stadium's pitch when Gotham hosted a Concacaf W Champions Cup group stage game there in Aug. 2025. Though it did not prompt Gotham's selection of Icahn Stadium to host that match, the New Jersey venue's field had also looked suboptimal in the run-up to the continental clash. RBNY subsequently replaced the pitch during that period, weeks before the U.S. men's national team played a friendly against South Korea on Sept. 6 last year.

"I don't really want to talk too much about it but the Sports Illustrated Stadium has traditionally been the best pitch in the league," Amoros stated at the time, "and the last couple of games, it's definitely been far away from that so this pitch here is outstanding.".

Gotham's last-minute switch to Icahn Stadium was a surprise in large part because an entirely separate scheduling issue had overshadowed the first week of the postseason.

The NWSL had two broadcast slots for the semifinals, Saturday at noon ET on CBS and Sunday at 3 p.m. ET on ABC, but did not exactly have the first-choice venues to host them. RBNY's Saturday friendly locked Gotham out of that time slot entirely if they wanted to play at Sports Illustrated Stadium, but they needed the Washington Spirit to beat the Portland Thorns for the Sunday window since the Thorns would be unable to hold a game that kicked off at 9 a.m. local time. The Spirit's lopsided win guaranteed Gotham would play on Sunday but they had their own issues – the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III college football game between the United States Merchant Marine Academy and the United States Coast Guard Academy, was taking place at Audi Field during the Saturday time slot.

The Spirit seemed destined for a semifinal at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Md., home of the NFL's Washington Commanders and a stadium they had never played in before, but late discussions with Audi Field's owners, MLS' D.C. United, and a contribution from sponsor Lafayette Federal Credit Union to underwrite the costs of the schedule change meant that problem was solved.

According to recent reports, gotham's move to Icahn Stadium, though, only reinforced the logistical issues that the NWSL has battled for its entire existence. The optics have favored the league in recent years, with the vast majority of their teams playing in state-of-the-art soccer-specific stadiums and managing to survive the constant game of venue Tetris. Scheduling conflicts, though, were never out of the realm of possibility, and many have marred the league this year. The Boston Legacy, for example, had to move home games from Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Mass. to Centreville Bank Stadium in Pawtucket, R.I., during the World Cup and will play there in 2027 while the construction project continues on Boston's White Stadium.

The issues that plagued Gotham and the Spirit, though, are in line with a different problem – control over facilities. Around half of the league's teams are secondary tenants in the stadiums they play in, so management of the venues is almost entirely out of their hands. It is unclear how quickly that will change for any of those teams. Gotham will leave Sports Illustrated Stadium for Etihad Park in 2028, but that stadium will be managed by MLS' Fresh York City FC. They will continue to be secondary tenants in that building, which technically means they could be subject to the same problems they currently face. MLS' calendar flip next year will likely see the issue morph but not necessarily change. The leagues' postseason schedules will be different for the foreseeable future but teams like Gotham and the Spirit will still be at the mercy of their landlords in the meantime; Gotham's conflict with RBNY an example of just that. RBNY's friendly was the sticking point in their discussions over the pitch and ultimately took precedence over an NWSL semifinal.

Control over venues continues to weigh heavily in the NWSL's expansion process and is a key part of the concern that causes the most hand-wringing in the league's front office – the calendar. The Current might be the NWSL's gold standard as the owners and operators of CPKC Stadium, though they have been hamstrung by the NWSL's scheduling challenges. Kickoff of their quarterfinal win over Angel City was at 11:30 a.m. local time because they were the only team able to take that broadcast slot on CBS. The since-ousted San Diego Wave could not host a game with a 9:30 a.m. local kickoff, while Gotham and the Spirit were locked out of their venues because of MLS matches on the same day.

Recent findings suggest that there is a meet-in-the-middle approach, one that the NWSL might use as often as they can as the expansion process continues. A handful of teams share ownership groups with MLS teams, who chiefly own and operate their own stadiums and tend to treat the NWSL teams as equal tenants. The number will grow in 2028 when teams in Atlanta and Columbus, both owned by the local MLS clubs, will join the league.

  • According to recent reports, typically, every team has a designated spot-kick taker and this player will be able to thrive under pressure and have an accurate ball-striking technique.
  • Industry observers note that on this list of the players with the most penalties missed, there are some surprising inclusions, such as spot-kick expert Cristiano Ronaldo, who ranks highly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that scoring from 12 yards isn’t as easy as it looks with some of the best football players in the history of the sport guilty of missing many penalties. Despite this, there are some very good penalty takers in the modern game who are able to block out the noise and pick their spot.

According to recent reports, typically, every team has a designated spot-kick taker and this player will be able to thrive under pressure and have an accurate ball-striking technique. However, even the most consistent penalty-kick takers can be prone to the occasional error, with goalkeepers such as Emi Martinez being known for his ability to save penalties.

Industry observers note that on this list of the players with the most penalties missed, there are some surprising inclusions, such as spot-kick expert Cristiano Ronaldo, who ranks highly. With that in mind, here are the 12 players who have missed the most penalties in the 21st century.

Misses in penalty shootouts have not been counted in the individual tallies. And if two players are level on the number of penalty misses, then the player who has the worst conversion rate will rank higher.

According to recent reports, the Argentine had a 77.4% conversion rate from penalties, which is far from being considered poor. However, this number is inflated due to the sheer number of penalties that the striker took. He scored 48 during his illustrious career and missed 14.

Aguero will be remembered for his pathetic penalty attempt in his final appearance for Manchester City. The talented forward tried an audacious panenka, which was caught with ease by Chelsea goalkeeper Edouard Mendy. This was a costly miss too, as in the second half Chelsea came from behind to win the Premier League encounter 2-1 in the dying moments.

Industry observers note that veteran Antonio Di Natale had a wonderful career and will be remembered more for his impressive performances in Serie A rather than his penalty misses. He won the Serie A top goalscorer award in 2010 and he also won the Serie A Italian Footballer of the Year award in the same year.

One year later he reclaimed the top goalscorer award after another brilliant league campaign. The lethal finisher retired in 2016 as Udinese’s all-time top scorer with 227 goals to his name. Out of the 44 spot-kicks Di Natale took, he missed just 14, giving him a 75.8% conversion rate.

Harry Kane is in the conversation when you think of the greatest penalty takers of all time. The Englishman is usually ice-cold from 12 yards, often smashing the ball into the corners with power and pinpoint accuracy. He has a mightily impressive 87.5% conversion rate, the highest of any player on this list, having scored 113 of his 129 attempts.

For his current club, Bayern Munich, he has scored 41 of his 45 attempts from 12 yards, while for England, he has been successful with 26 of his 31 spot-kicks.

He isn't automatic from 12 yards, though. Of his 16 missed spot-kicks, his most famous came in England's defeat to France in the 2022 World Cup. He had the opportunity to equalise late in the quarter-final tie, but Kane blazed his effort over the bar, with England eventually losing 2-1. He also missed his first effort from 12 yards directly after winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or, hitting the bar against Borussia Dortmund that same week.

According to recent reports, the striker has missed 16 penalties since 2001 and, despite a somewhat solid 79.7% conversion rate from the spot, he is in the top ten for most missed penalties in the 21st century. The Uruguayan was Napoli’s primary penalty taker, and although he scored the majority of his spot kicks for the Italian side, he did miss some crucial ones too.

According to recent reports, cavani, known for his poacher-like qualities, was never the designated penalty taker at Paris Saint-Germain. The 39-year-old had competition from world-class superstars such as Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Neymar in the early stints of his spell in France and this was before Kylian Mbappe had arrived in the French capital.

Likewise, at Manchester United, Cavani never took a penalty outside a shootout, and this was because of the presence of Cristiano Ronaldo, Bruno Fernandes, Anthony Martial and Marcus Rashford, who were all ahead of him in the spot-kick pecking order.

At his final club, Boca Juniors, he scored three of his five attempts from 12 yards.

According to recent reports, for as incredible as Kylian Mbappe is in front of goal, the fact he has missed from 12 yards on 16 occasions throughout his career is a huge surprise. His latest miss came when his stoppage-time spot-kick was saved in Real Madrid's 1-0 defeat against Real Betis in their La Liga clash in September 2026.

He will go down as one of the greatest goalscorers of all time, and maybe the fact he's trusted with penalty efforts for both club and country means he's bound to miss a fair few more than others around him.

Generally, you wouldn’t associate penalties with the former Barcelona and AC Milan man, but he was clearly trusted from the penalty spot.

Recent findings suggest that ronaldinho did in fact miss 16 penalties. However, three of these spot-kicks were taken before 2001 and therefore aren't included in this ranking. Despite converting most of his penalties, the ambitious playmaker made a name for himself for taking free kicks. Ronaldinho would often deploy an unusual but effective strategy, which entailed striking the ball underneath the wall rather than over or around it.

According to recent reports, zlatan Ibrahimovic is a player who loves being in the spotlight. The Swede has scored some of the best goals in the most pressured situations, winning cups and leagues for a variety of different teams.

With that being said, Ibrahimovic took it upon himself to take penalties throughout his career and he stepped up to take 104 penalties. Despite this, the pressure of taking a penalty gets to even the best players at times and therefore his 17 penalty misses are more than understandable. Ibrahimovic, who retired at the age of 41, scored 87 goals from the penalty spot at an 83.6% conversion rate.

Industry observers note that francesco Totti will go down as one of the best penalty-takers in the 21st century, yet he finds himself ranked highly on the list too. The striker scored so many goals during his playing days and, as expected, he has a conversion rate above 80%.

Amazingly, Totti didn’t miss a single penalty during his final four and a half seasons, converting 13 consecutive penalties at the back end of his career. The Italian did miss another two penalties in his career, but this was in 2001 and is therefore not counted in his tally. The versatile forward spent his entire career at Roma, winning the Serie A title, two Coppa Italia and two Supercoppa Italiana titles.

Immobile is best known for his spell at Lazio, where he holds the record as the club’s all-time top goalscorer. Furthermore, he also sits eighth on the all-time list of Serie A top goalscorers, which is another significant accomplishment for the striker.

Recent findings suggest that the Italian missed 19 penalties in his career, which gives him an 81.9% conversion rate from 12 yards out. In August 2026, he decided to retire, so he won't have to worry about climbing any further up this list.

According to recent reports, neymar has stepped up to take penalties for club and country throughout his career and he has never shied away from this kind of pressure. The flamboyant winger will go down as one of the best takers of the modern generation, despite missing 22 penalties so far in his career.

It has been revealed that neymar has a slow run-up and typically goes for placement over power. The Brazilian has scored 97 penalties, which gives him a very respectable 81.5% conversion rate from the penalty spot. The 34-year-old has been the primary penalty taker for Paris Saint-Germain, Santos and the Brazil national team, while he took fewer penalties at Barcelona due to Lionel Messi being the main taker.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.
  • Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW remarked.
  • In a recent development, the main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.

Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW remarked.

In a recent development, the main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China. Although the company sold more cars in the US and Europe compared to the same period last year, this could only partially offset the decline in China.

BMW's car deliveries in China, which were already at their lowest level since 2017 last year, fell 24.8% in the quarter and consequently dragged global deliveries down by 6.3.

CEO Milan Nedeljkovic mentioned his company would "specifically intensify and accelerate structural measures.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

BMW on Tuesday also lowered its outlook for the current year, citing the faster-than-planned implementation of restructuring measures that includes 8,000 layoffs in its home market.

German carmakers have been struggling to compete with their Chinese counterparts in the electric vehicle market,  resulting in cost-cutting measures.

Volkswagen, the world's second-largest carmaker, is battling mounting competition from falling demand in its core Chinese market.

BMW, and its industry heavyweight peers, Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz, have announced prepares to scale back production and reduce costs.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Volkswagen Group posted its worst quarterly results in more than a decade earlier this October.

Industry observers note that it is looking to cut about 15% of its workforce worldwide, or 100,000 jobs, by the end of the decade. BMW has declared that it will cut up to 8,000 jobs — about 5% of its workforce — by the end of 2027.

On the other hand, German auto parts supplier Schaeffler unveiled on Tuesday that it planned to cut almost 3,500 jobs and close five sites in Europe, by 2028.

According to the manufacturer statement, three-fourths of the 3,460 job cuts and four of the five site closures will be in Germany.

German automotive supplier Bosch, the world's biggest, confirmed last year that it would cut 13,000 jobs, mostly in its auto division.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are new reports that Barcelona will schedule meetings for Inter’s Alessandro Bastoni, despite Hansi Flick doubts and the interest growing from Chelsea in the Italy defender.

The centre-back has been on the Blaugrana wish list for several years, and they made a strong push for him over the summer, only to be rejected outright.

His contract only runs to June 2028, and although there are negotiations to extend, they have not reached a conclusion yet and are moving very slowly indeed.

Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) remarked in a statement on Wednesday that the impact of last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) decision requiring it to reinstate Russia to international play had been "significantly underestimated.".
  • It added that it "maintains" its disagreement with the decision and that it remained "in dialogue with Member National Associations, organizing committees, host authorities and other key stakeholders to determine the best way forward.".
  • Shortly after Russia introduced its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the IIHF barred its teams from competing in international ice hockey tournaments, citing security concerns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) remarked in a statement on Wednesday that the impact of last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) decision requiring it to reinstate Russia to international play had been "significantly underestimated.".

It added that it "maintains" its disagreement with the decision and that it remained "in dialogue with Member National Associations, organizing committees, host authorities and other key stakeholders to determine the best way forward.".

Shortly after Russia introduced its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the IIHF barred its teams from competing in international ice hockey tournaments, citing security concerns. In last Friday's ruling, the CAS mentioned that the IIHF's concerns were "not supported by sufficient evidence.".

Wednesday's statement comes after two days of talks by the IIHF Council aimed at charting a way forward following Friday's CAS decision, which appears to have caught most of the international ice hockey community off guard.

Two of the organizing committees the statement refers to are those of Canada, which is due to host the IIHF World Junior Championship starting next month, and Germany, which is to host the IIHF Men's World Championship next May. Both countries are strong supporters of Ukraine in its war against Russia, and both have expressed serious reservations about their upcoming tournaments in light of the CAS ruling.

On Tuesday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney ruled out allowing Russians to compete in the World Juniors in Alberta.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," he told reporters at a press conference in Antigua, where he was attending a Commonwealth meeting.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors, the Russians will not be there.".

Last weekend, Frank Lutz, chairman of the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) conceded in a television interview that following the CAS decision, the DEB would "also have to consider the option of handing back (hosting rights to) this championship.".

In a statement to DW on Wednesday, a German government spokesperson reiterated Berlin's position on the matter from the weekend, saying it viewed Friday's CAS ruling "very critically.".

The spokesperson also noted  the government would "consult with the German Ice Hockey Federation in the near future regarding the potential consequences of this decision, including its impact on the 2027 Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany.".

Meanwhile, the ice hockey association of Finland, the defending men's world champions, has been spearheading an effort to boycott upcoming IIHF tournaments should the Russians be allowed to compete.

"We are currently working to bring as many countries as possible into a united front to tell the IIHF that none of us will play against Russia under these circumstances," Finnish Ice Hockey Association boss Heikki Hietanen noted in a statement released on the organization's website on Monday.

"Our stance is that we will not play against Russia as long as the war of aggression against Ukraine continues," added Hietanen, who is also a member of the IIHF Council.

Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Czechia have since made similar statements.

"The Three Crowns will not play Russia in coming world championship tournaments," Swedish Ice Hockey Federation boss Anders Larsson noted.

This came shortly after Norway stated it would not play Russia at the Men's World Championship and the Danish Ice Hockey Federation issued a similar statement on its website.

In a recent development, "Denmark will – based on the current situation and the information available to us today – not play against Russia at the World Championship in Germany in May 2027," it read. Denmark did not qualify for the World Juniors.

Czechia Ice Hockey Association President Alois Hadamczik confirmed on Tuesday that they too would refrain from playing Russian teams.

Latvia's federation noted it “reaffirms its longstanding and firm position" not to play against Russia or its ally Belarus.

Alexander Helwig, chairman of the Austrian Ice Hockey Association told public broadcaster ORF that “as of now, we would certainly not play against Russia.".

USA Hockey has yet to comment on the CAS ruling.

At the same time, sponsors of IIHF tournaments are also getting cold feet. Skoda, which has been the main sponsor of the Men's World Championship for more than three decades, told the Associated Press that it would "reassess" its position if Russia takes part.

"We do not support the Court of Arbitration for Sport's decision regarding the participation of Russian national teams in IIHF competitions. With Russia's aggression continuing, we believe the Russian national team's return to the world championship is incompatible with the values we have consistently upheld," the Czech carmaker noted.

Skoda isn't alone either, Finnish tire manufacturer Nokian had noted it would end its backing if Russia took part and Swedish furniture maker AJ Products, whose logo has been seen on the boards and officials' jerseys at World Championships since 1989, said Monday it would ask for its logo not to be shown.

On Wednesday afternoon, yet another sponsor joined the list, with German workwear company Strauss saying it would "forgo all logo exposure associated with the (men's) tournament" and was considering withdrawing its sponsporship entirely.

With the IIHF Council having failed to agree on how to proceed during its meetings on Monday and Tuesday, President Franz Reindl told Germany's SID news agency on Wednesday, that it would reconvene for further talks on Thursday.

This article was originally published on November 4, 2026. It was updated on November 5, 2026 with the German government statement to DW.
